subject: function libraries with the C++ preprocessor

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: function libraries with the C++ preprocessor
parts:
Hi!

A feature I have been long missing in Stan are function libraries. I just found this ticket here:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/810

in where Daniel suggests to simply run

g++ -E -x c++ foo.stan

to get a parsed Stan file which has #include statements being executed. I just tried this and it apparently seems to work just fine. Is there any caveat here except that I may not use "#" as a comment character?

This will reduce my copy-and-pasting need a lot. Thanks much for any hints here.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: function libraries with the C++ preprocessor
parts:
Hi!

For anyone who wants to use this include stuff with cmdstan more systematic: Just add into make/local two lines like

%.stan : %.tstan
        $(CC) -x c++ -E $< -o $@

Note, that the space before "$(CC)" must be a tab! Then you can write in the future instead of .stan files .tstan files. When you build the model executables as usual, the above make rule will turn the .tstan in a .stan file file the pre-processor being run over it. You may want to toss in some more options to your preprocessor to point the program to a location where you stored you to-be-included stan snippets, haven't figure that out.

If you want to continue use # as comment character, then you would have to add in another sed command above.

I find it really useful, but this is not a "Stan-standard".

Cheers,
Sebastian
